sections.html:
Leesburg is in Lake County, and the city runs its own electric, gas, water and wastewater utilities. A sale therefore involves city utility accounts as well as county tax records. Whether you plan to list, sell alone or take a cash offer, sort out both sets of paperwork early.

  • An agent listing works for a sound house and a long runway.
  • A by-owner sale needs you to run showings, contracts and disclosures.
  • A cash buyer suits a house where repairs, renters or liens drive the schedule.

Leesburg is Lake County's oldest city, incorporated on July 12, 1875. It takes its name from Calvin Lee, whose brother Evander Lee settled the area in 1857. The city commission form of government dates to the 1922 charter, and Venetian Gardens on the lakefront began as a project in 1938. Buyers drawn by water access or events often start near the lakefront and downtown, so say how far your house is from both.

sections.h2: Storms, cold snaps and water limits
sections.html:
Storm history comes up in inspections, insurance quotes and buyer questions. The city closed city facilities for Hurricane Helene and Hurricane Milton in September and October 2024 and earlier for Hurricane Ian in 2022. Lake County issued a countywide burn ban in March 2025, and the city has handed out sandbags ahead of storms.

In early 2026 a historic freeze led the city to post cold-weather tips, a good reminder to check pipes, irrigation lines and older heating systems before showings. In May 2026 a Phase III Extreme Water Shortage notice came from the St. Johns water district, so ask the city and the district what lawn and irrigation limits apply when you list.

Put storm repair receipts and insurance claim papers in a single folder. A cash buyer will price whatever repairs remain, and a financed buyer's lender may ask for proof of the fixes. Add a few sentences on how the house fared.

sections.h2: Lake County offices, exemptions and key dates
sections.html:
The county property appraiser sets values and decides exemptions, and a separate county tax collector sends bills and takes payment. Value is set January 1, a proposed-tax notice arrives in August, and bills come in November.

A homestead exemption can reach $50,000. The first $25,000 applies to all taxes, including school taxes, and a second layer of up to $25,000 applies to value above $50,000 and only to non-school taxes (s. 196.031).

Dates for a Leesburg homeowner
DateWhat to do or expect
March 1Exemption filing deadline
March 31Homestead tax deferral application (Form DR-570)
April 1Unpaid taxes become delinquent
May 1Leesburg fire assessment exemption applications due

The city posts its fire assessment exemption notice each winter. Ask the city how the assessment is handled on a sale so it does not surprise either side.

sections.h2: Protecting your title from deed fraud
sections.html:
The Lake County Property Appraiser warns that scammers record phony deeds to appear as owners, then take money from people who believe they are renting or buying.

The Lake County Clerk of the Court runs a free alert that e-mails you when anything is filed in the official records under a name you monitor, for as many as 5 names per address. Owners of vacant Leesburg houses and heirs who live elsewhere benefit most. Sign up before you list so any strange filing against the property reaches you quickly.

sections.h2: Can back taxes cost me a Leesburg house?
sections.html:
A bill left unpaid goes delinquent on April 1. By June 1 the county sells a certificate against it to an investor. That investor must wait until two years after April 1 of the issue year before pressing the owner.

Then the investor can apply for a tax deed by paying a $75 fee (s. 197.502). If the land is homestead, the opening bid includes one-half of the latest assessed value plus what is owed. Request a full statement of amounts due from the Lake County tax collector before you list.

A homestead owner with a tight budget can file Form DR-570 by March 31 after the assessment year to defer the portion of the bill above 5 percent of last year's household income. The threshold is 3 percent for a permanent resident 65 or older.

Leesburg announced in August 2025 that building permit fees would rise in October, so a renovation you planned to permit may cost more than older figures suggest.

The Florida Department of Transportation has run work on US 27 from CR 33 to Middlesex Road and on SR 44 at South Street. Buyers drive a street before they bid, so a project near your address can come up in negotiation. Ask the city about open permits on the address, and give any past owner-built work to the buyer in writing.

sections.h2: What to fix before showing a Leesburg house
sections.html:
Tour the house the way a buyer would, curb to back fence. Start with fixes that cost little: loose handrails, stained ceiling tiles, dripping faucets and broken screens. Pull together utility bills, storm repair receipts and warranty papers.

Test smoke alarms and check the electrical safety of older wiring before listing. A clean inspection report helps hold your price, and it shows buyers you kept up with the house. Because Leesburg's utilities are city-run, schedule the final reads for water, gas and electric around your closing date.

  • Smoke alarms tested and batteries replaced.
  • Roof, plumbing and electrical panel dates written down.
  • Irrigation timers set to the rules in force.
  • Final utility reads booked for the closing date.

After you accept an offer, the title company searches the record for mortgages, judgments and unpaid taxes. You then review a settlement statement and sign the deed. On the closing date, move the city electric, gas and water accounts to the buyer and file your last bills with the sale papers. A buyer's agent will usually ask when each meter was read.

If a tenant lives in the house, tell the buyer in writing whether the lease stays or ends. Bring ID, the payoff figure from your lender and the names of everyone on the deed to the signing.

sections.h2: Weighing a listing against a cash offer
sections.html:
Write both options down as the cash you would keep. For a listing, start with the expected price, then take away the agent's commission, repairs a buyer's inspector will request, and the months of insurance, taxes and utilities you pay while the house sits on the market. For a cash offer, subtract only the fees the contract hands to you.

A sound, updated house with time to wait often does better on the market. A house with deferred repairs, a tenant or a lien tends to move faster to a buyer who closes as is. Ask for the deposit, the closing date and the title company in writing, and never pay a fee just to receive an offer.

faqs.a: July 12, 1875, about a dozen years before Lake County was formed.

faqs.q: Who values my Leesburg home for tax purposes?
faqs.a: The Lake County Property Appraiser sets value each January 1 and rules on exemptions, while the tax collector sends bills. Exemption claims are due March 1.

faqs.q: Can I monitor for fraudulent deeds on my property?
faqs.a: Yes, through a free Lake County Clerk of the Court e-mail alert covering up to 5 names per address.

faqs.q: When do unpaid property taxes become delinquent?
faqs.a: On April 1. A certificate is then sold by June 1, and its holder may seek a tax deed two years after April 1 of the issue year (s. 197.502).

faqs.q: Which utilities does the city of Leesburg run?
faqs.a: Electric, gas, water and wastewater, so utility transfers at closing go through the city.
